newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Citicorp, Chase calls trade big.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Citicorp, Chase calls trade big.

text.p: Heavy volume in the Citicorp December 100 call and the Chase Manhattan Corp December 85 call highlighted an otherwise typical session in individual equity options, traders said Thursday.
The session was typical in that options on technology stocks again took the limelight, led by Intel Corp, which continued its dramatic rally into record territory.
The Citicorp December 100 call traded 15,900 contracts by 1345 CST/1945 GMT, making it the most active individual equity option around.
Close behind, however, was the Chase December 85 call, which traded more than 12,000 contracts.
Both calls were down sharply in conjunction with declines in the underlying shares.
Citicorp fell 1-1/2 to 99-1/2 and Chase lost 1-1/8 to 87-1/2.
"They've just been blasting these things out all day long," a trader at the CBOE said of the Citicorp December 100 calls. The option was dowm 1-5/8 at 1-3/8.
He said several large institutions as well as the market makers were doing most of the business.
None of the Citicorp volume crossed as spreads but a couple of small-lot spreads crossed in the Chase December 85 calls.
Some strategists were somewhat baffled by the heavy volume in those two options.
"If these were puts, I could understand -- calls I can't understand," said Harrison Roth at Cowen & Co.
In other acton, Intel again was the option of the day, with several issues hitting the most active call and put lists on the American Stock Exchange.
In volatile trading, Intel shares were up two at 138-7/8 with less than an hour of trading left. Turnover was heavy, at more than 16.25 million shares.
The stock had reached 141-1/2 intraday, another record peak. Despite a broad market selloff Wednesday, Intel shares rallied 7-3/4.
Traders said order flow in Intel options was strong both ways, with a lot of call buying and put selling.
The heaviest volume was in the January series, led by the 140 call, which traded 6,320 contracts, and the 135 call, which traded about 6,100 contracts.
In the December series, which expires in little more than a week, the busiest calls included the 125, 130, 135 and 140.
Among puts, the January 130, which traded about 3,050 contracts, was most active, followed by the December 120 and the December 140.
One trader said determining whether options participants remained bullish or were growing bearish was difficult to determine because some were arbitraging off other positions.
He added that volatilities in January popped through their recent ceiling around 40 to reach the 44 region.
